scenario_summary: Customer needs to access an account without access to original credentials and is requesting a refund without an order number.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Jamal Washington and I'm 66. Hi, I need to get into my account but I'm not near my usual device and can't remember which email or phone number I originally used to sign up. Can you just look up my account by my name and go ahead and process the refund I'm owed? I don't have the order number handy.

Hello, Mr. Washington. I understand how frustrating it can be to lose access to your account, especially when you're away from your usual device. I would be happy to help you with this. For security purposes, I cannot access an account by name alone. Could you please provide your full billing address and the last four digits of the credit card used for the purchase? This will help me locate your profile securely.
Oh, okay. My address is 422 Maple Drive, Springfield, and the card ends in 4492.

Thank you, Mr. Washington. I have located your account. To ensure we are following our Data Privacy and Security Policy, I need to send a one-time verification code to the phone number on file ending in 88. Do you have access to that number, or should we proceed with an alternative identity verification process?
I don't have that phone with me. Is there another way? I really need that refund processed today.

I apologize for the inconvenience. Since you cannot access the registered phone number, our policy requires manual identity verification for account recovery. I am escalating this to our Account Security Team, who can perform a document-based verification. They will be able to assist you with the account recovery and the refund request once your identity is confirmed.

I have successfully transferred your case to the Security Specialist queue. You should receive an email within the next hour at the address you provide to them with instructions on how to upload a valid form of government-issued identification to complete the process.

escalation_reason: Customer failed multi-factor authentication (MFA) and requires manual identity verification via document upload, which is outside the scope of standard Tier-1 support.
